title: Enforce auto eligibility and record autonomous authority
name: auto-eligibility
description: Implement the selected authority boundary so auto can act only under explicit invocation, with zero open decisions anywhere on the board. Recheck before brief approval, dispatch and acceptance; refuse missing or malformed board state, overlaps, claims, stale decisions, unsafe base (including main) and missing verification. Record that approval and acceptance were autonomous rather than attributing them to an unobserved human. Include tests for concurrent board changes and the attended path.

brief.approach:
Implement ADR 0065 §2–§7 in core only; the `sober:auto` entry point, its skill and auto-reject sequencing belong to auto-lifecycle-jo8f and auto-skill-g9sj.

1. Provenance in the schema. Add `AutoProvenance = z.strictObject({ invocation: z.literal('sober:auto'), invokedBy: Handle })` in packages/schema/src (beside `Approval` in brief.ts, or a small auto.ts re-exported from the index). Add `autonomous: AutoProvenance.optional()` to `Approval` (packages/schema/src/brief.ts) and `Accepted` (packages/schema/src/node.ts). Optional, not defaulted, so every existing record parses and is not rewritten; absent means a human did it. `by` on an autonomous record is the invoker's handle, and the record says it was automated — never read as that person's approval.

2. The gate, packages/core/src/auto.ts (new). `autoGate(board, node, transition: 'approve' | 'dispatch' | 'accept', base)` returns a list of refusal reasons, empty when clear; `AutoRefusedError extends SoberError` (code `auto-refused`) carries them. Checks, all from a fresh `loadBoard` (packages/core/src/graph.ts), never a cached board: `openDecisions(board)` empty board-wide (status.ts — drafts count as open); `board.broken` empty and `findCycle(board.nodes)` null; `statusOf` equals the transition's expected status (approve → a written, unapproved brief; dispatch → ready; accept → in-review); no `claim` by anyone other than the invoker; `overlaps(board.nodes, node)` (team.ts) empty; `flagsOf(board, node)` not stale-flagged; brief present with a non-empty acceptance list; base safe (see 4); and for dispatch, no retry (see 5).

3. Auto transitions, same file. `autoApprove(paths, node, { invokedBy, base })`, `autoDispatch(paths, node, { invokedBy, base, ... })`, `autoAccept(paths, node, { invokedBy, base, scan, ci })`. Each reuses the attended mechanics rather than copying them: `approveBrief` (decide.ts) and `acceptWork` (review.ts) gain an optional `autonomous?: AutoProvenance` option written into the record, and an optional `guard?: () => Promise<void>` awaited inside their existing lock right before writing/merging. The auto functions pass `guard` = reload board + `autoGate`, so a decision opened, a claim taken, a record broken or an overlapping node started between the caller's check and the write is caught. autoDispatch calls `dispatch` (dispatch.ts) with `anyway` and `attended` never set. Attended callers pass neither option and behave exactly as today; the attended surfaces (MCP `approve`/`accept`, CLI, server routes) must not be able to set `autonomous`. Events appended with the provenance.

4. Unsafe base. Auto requires `dispatch.base` in config (packages/core/src/config.ts) to be set; `base` must equal it, and must not be `main`, `master` or match `release/*` / `release-*`. A null `dispatch.base` refuses with a sentence saying to set it. Nothing here opens a PR into main or writes a changeset.

5. No retry (ADR 0056 decision 3). autoDispatch refuses when the node has any prior run that failed, timed out or was stopped, or any rejection feedback (`lastRun`, `board.feedback`): it is the human's from then on.

6. Accept threshold (§5). autoAccept requires `scan === 'clean'`, `auditOf(paths, node) === 'passed'` (`none`/`did-not-run`/`failed` refuse), CI `passed` where the project has CI (unreadable → refuse), and not flagged. Anything short refuses with the reason and leaves the node in review; it does not reject (that sequencing is auto-lifecycle's).

7. Rendering. Every surface that prints an approval or acceptance says when it was autonomous, e.g. `approved autonomously under sober:auto (invoked by X)`: packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts (brief tool), packages/mcp/src/render.ts (review header), packages/cli/src/work.ts and review.ts, apps/dashboard/src/panel/Panel.tsx and apps/dashboard/src/review/data.ts. No new MCP tool and no CLI command in this node.

8. Export the new API from packages/core/src/index.ts and update the exports snapshot. Tests: packages/core/src/auto.test.ts covering each refusal (open decision elsewhere on the board, draft decision, archived decision ignored, broken record, cycle, claimed by another, overlap, stale flag, missing brief, null base, `main`, release branch, retry after failure/rejection, each inconclusive accept input), provenance written and parsed, a change landing after the gate passes but before the locked write (a decision opened in that window) refusing without writing, and old records without `autonomous` still loading. Schema tests in packages/schema/src/brief.test.ts and node.test.ts for the optional strict field. test/integration/attended.test.ts gains a case proving the attended approve/dispatch path writes no `autonomous` field and is not held by an open decision elsewhere on the board; test/integration/review.test.ts proves an attended accept writes none either and an autonomous accept records it after a real merge.

acceptance.proves: The gate refuses every ADR 0065 §3–§5 condition from a fresh board read, rechecks under the write lock so a concurrent change is caught, and records autonomous provenance on approval and acceptance.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/decide.test.ts packages/core/src/exports.test.ts
acceptance.proves: Attended approval is unchanged for callers that pass no autonomous option, and the new core API is exported deliberately.
Existing records without the provenance field still parse and the new field is strict.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec vitest run --project integration test/integration/attended.test.ts test/integration/review.test.ts
acceptance.proves: The attended approve, dispatch and accept paths write no autonomous record and are not held by the auto-only board-wide rule, while an autonomous accept records provenance after a real merge.
Schema, core, MCP, CLI and dashboard compile with the new optional fields.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec biome check packages/core/src packages/schema/src packages/mcp/src packages/cli/src apps/dashboard/src test/integration/attended.test.ts test/integration/review.test.ts
acceptance.proves: Changed files pass repository style checks.
